sentences.text: Plagiophthalmosuchus was a small marine predator that hunted fish.
Scientists named this genus in 2020, moving the species gracilirostris from Steneosaurus.
Its jaws produced a relatively weak but fast bite.
A narrow snout minimized water resistance for precise, rapid strikes, while teeth suited for gripping rather than crushing.
This animal lived between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago in the Early Toarcian stage.
Its remains were found in what is now Whitby, Yorkshire, UK, and Dudelange, Luxembourg.
A 2024 study suggests Plagiophthalmosuchus may belong outside Teleosauroidea as one of the most basal thalattosuchians, contradicting its earlier classification.
